name: NW General Examples
miniText: How do network generation rules and graph direction affect the statistics reported for the same displayed nodes? NetLogo NW General Examples combines network generators, layouts, clusterers, and measurements from the NW extension. Watts and Strogatz [1] supply the small-world mechanism, Barabási and Albert [2] supply preferential growth, and Brandes [3] develops efficient betweenness centrality. The baseline exposes these distinct tasks through shared controls, making it important to distinguish topology from screen layout and generation from analysis. The original Info warns that selecting the wrong directed-link context can produce misleading zero measurements. Disconnected components, link types, and chosen generator parameters also change meaning. The example illustrates public graph capabilities and their assumptions; an attractive layout is not evidence of a small-world property, and successful measurement does not validate a network model against real social or urban data.
